## What is metapropul? {-}

**metapropul** is an R package designed for systematic reviewers who need to
conduct and report meta-analyses without wrestling with low-level statistical
plumbing. It wraps the battle-tested `meta` and `metafor` engines behind a
clean, consistent interface guided by one simple philosophy:

> *Beginners get everything with minimal code. Experts opt out rather than opt in.*

All sensible defaults are on. Customisation is available but never required.

## What can you do? {-}

<div class="card-grid">

<div class="card">
<span class="card-icon">📊</span>
<h4>Pool Effect Sizes</h4>
<p>Odds ratios, risk ratios, hazard ratios, mean differences, and proportions — all with one function call.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<span class="card-icon">🌲</span>
<h4>Forest Plots</h4>
<p>Publication-ready forest plots with automatic sizing, subgroup panels, and multiple layout styles.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<span class="card-icon">🔍</span>
<h4>Publication Bias</h4>
<p>Egger's test, Begg's test, trim-and-fill, contour-enhanced funnel plots, and limit meta-analysis.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<span class="card-icon">📐</span>
<h4>Heterogeneity</h4>
<p>I², τ², leave-one-out plots, and Baujat plots to understand between-study variation.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<span class="card-icon">📉</span>
<h4>Influence Analysis</h4>
<p>Leave-one-out diagnostics — forest plots and summary tables — to spot influential studies.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<span class="card-icon">📋</span>
<h4>Summary Tables</h4>
<p>gt-powered tables formatted for direct copy-paste into Word or PDF manuscripts.</p>
</div>

</div>

## Quick start {-}

```r
# Install from GitHub (CRAN submission pending)
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("drrubesh/metapropul")

library(metapropul)

# --- Proportions in 3 lines ---
data(dat_bcg, package = "metapropul")
result <- meta_prop(dat_bcg, event = "tpos", n = "npos", studylab = "author")
forest_meta(result)
```
